extracted.intended_audience: general readers and historians interested in Benjamin Franklin / colonial administration
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts and recounts episodes of Benjamin Franklin's public life: proposals for city sanitation, postal administration, logistics and contracting for military service, and colonial political measures. The page is an excerpt from Franklin's autobiography describing concrete procedural proposals and practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Street sanitation and mud removal
rubrics_metrics.description: That the mud, when rak'd up, be not left in heaps to be spread abroad again by the wheels of carriages and trampling of horses, but that the scavengers be provided with bodies of carts, not plac'd high upon wheels, but low upon sliders, with lattice bottoms, which, being cover'd with straw, will retain the mud thrown into them, and permit the water to drain from it, whereby it will become much lighter...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bring the mud to low-bodied carts with lattice bottoms (covered with straw) by wheelbarrows; leave the carts in place until the mud has drained (water being most of its weight), then have horses draw them away. Franklin notes doubts about practicability in very narrow streets but endorses sweeping dust up and carrying it away before shops open in summer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sweep dust before shops open (timing of cleaning)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requiring the dust to be swept up and carry'd away before the shops are open
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Franklin considers this practicable in summer when days are long; he observes many inhabitants choose to live by candlelight and thus shops often open late, making early-morning sweeping feasible and effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of small practical improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: Human felicity is produc'd not so much by great pieces of good fortune that seldom happen, as by little advantages that occur every day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Franklin argues that small, practical improvements (example: teaching a poor young man to shave and keep his razor) yield more lasting happiness than large but transient gifts (example: a thousand guineas). This is offered as a principle for prioritizing everyday civic improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-office administration: implement profitable improvements despite initial cost
rubrics_metrics.description: Having been ... comptroller in regulating several offices ... To do this, a variety of improvements were necessary; some of these were inevitably at first expensive, so that in the first four years the office became above nine hundred pounds in debt to us. But it soon after began to repay us; and before I was displac'd ... we had brought it to yield three times as much clear revenue to the crown as the postoffice of Ireland.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Franklin presents a managerial criterion: identify and implement systemic improvements even if initially costly, because they can convert a loss-making office into a highly profitable one; keep officers accountable and regulate offices to produce clear revenue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design of a colonial union (Albany Plan)
rubrics_metrics.description: By this plan the general government was to be administered by a president-general, appointed and supported by the crown, and a grand council was to be chosen by the representatives of the people of the several colonies, met in their respective assemblies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Franklin's plan was intended to centralize defense and common purposes while combining crown-appointed executive with a council chosen by colonial representatives. He records objections: assemblies considered it to give too much prerogative; in England it was judged too democratic, showing the rubric of balancing prerogative and representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vet proposals with knowledgeable peers before public presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: As we pass'd thro' New York, I had there shown my project to Mr. James Alexander and Mr. Kennedy, two gentlemen of great knowledge in public affairs, and, being fortified by their approbation, I ventur'd to lay it before the Congress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Franklin recommends consulting informed, reputable colleagues to test and strengthen a proposal before presenting it to a larger political body; their approbation lends weight and confidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finance public purchases via Loan Office orders (short-term interest-bearing instruments)
rubrics_metrics.description: I then suggested a method of doing the business without the governor, by orders on the trustees of the Loan Office, which, by law, the Assembly had the right of drawing. There was, indeed, little or no money at that time in the office, and therefore I propos'd that the orders should be payable in a year, and to bear an interest of five per cent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use legally-authorized short-term interest-bearing orders to finance urgent public purchases when cash is scarce; such orders can obtain instant credit and circulate as money if backed by reliable funds (e.g., loan interest and excise revenue).

rubrics_metrics.name: Waggon and horse hire: explicit payment rates
rubrics_metrics.description: That there shall be paid for each waggon, with four good horses and a driver, fifteen shillings per diem; and for each able horse with a pack-saddle, or other saddle and furniture, two shillings per diem; and for each able horse without a saddle, eighteen pence per diem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish explicit, itemized daily compensation rates in any public contract advertisement to standardize expectations and facilitate rapid enlistment of resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract: commencement of pay and travel allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: That the pay commence from the time of their joining the forces at Will's Creek ... and that a reasonable allowance be paid over and above for the time necessary for their travelling to Will's Creek and home again after their discharge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define precisely when pay begins (e.g., time of joining the service) and include allowances for travel time to and from the service location to make offers attractive and fair.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract: valuation and compensation for loss
rubrics_metrics.description: Each waggon and team, and every saddle or pack horse, is to be valued by indifferent persons chosen between me and the owner; and in case of the loss of any waggon, team, or other horse in the service, the price according to such valuation is to be allowed and paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a neutral appraisal mechanism (indifferent persons chosen by both parties) and guarantee compensation for loss according to that valuation to reduce dispute and encourage participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract: advance payment and settlement
rubrics_metrics.description: Seven days' pay is to be advanced and paid in hand by me to the owner of each waggon and team, or horse, at the time of contracting, if required, and the remainder to be paid by General Braddock, or by the paymaster of the army, at the time of their discharge, or from time to time, as it shall be demanded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer a short upfront advance to contractors to secure commitment and require remaining payment on discharge or demand; specify responsible payors (contracting agent vs. army paymaster).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract: ensure hired civilians are not pressed into soldier duties
rubrics_metrics.description: No drivers of waggons, or persons taking care of the hired horses, are on any account to be called upon to do the duty of soldiers, or be otherwise employed than in conducting or taking care of their carriages or horses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include explicit contractual protections that hired logistical personnel will not be conscripted for combat or other duties beyond their hiring terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract: army may take surplus forage with reasonable compensation
rubrics_metrics.description: All oats, Indian corn, or other forage that waggons or horses bring to the camp, more than is necessary for the subsistence of the horses, is to be taken for the use of the army, and a reasonable price paid for the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate and specify terms for requisitioning surplus supplies for military use, assuring owners of reasonable compensation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Owners may require a bond for contractor's performance
rubrics_metrics.description: The owners, however, alleging they did not know General Braddock, or what dependence might be had on his promise, insisted on my bond for the performance, which I accordingly gave them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the payor or principal is not known or trusted by suppliers, require a local bond or guaranty from the contracting intermediary to secure performance and reassure resource providers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition of officer relief parcels (provisions for officers)
rubrics_metrics.description: These twenty parcels, well pack'd, were placed on as many horses, each parcel, with the horse, being intended as a present for one officer. They consisted of: 6 lbs. loaf sugar; 6 lbs. good Muscovado; 1 Gloucester cheese; 1 keg containing 20 lbs. good butter; 1 lb. good green tea; 2 doz. old Madeira wine; ... vinegar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Franklin provides a detailed contents list as a template for a single officer's relief parcel (sugars, cheeses, butter, tea, wine, spirits, coffee, chocolate, biscuits, spices, mustard, hams, tongues, rice, raisins, etc.), suitable for nourishment and morale on campaign.

rubrics_metrics.name: Military logistics: avoid long, slender marching formations in narrow roads
rubrics_metrics.description: The slender line, near four miles long, which your army must make, may expose it to be attack'd by surprise in its flanks, and to be cut like a thread into several pieces, which, from their distance, can not come up in time to support each other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When planning marches through woods or narrow roads, avoid extended single-file or very long lines that expose flanks and prevent units from supporting each other; anticipate ambuscade tactics and arrange formations to reduce vulnerability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat allied scouts kindly to retain their service
rubrics_metrics.description: George Croghan, our Indian interpreter, join'd him on his march with one hundred of those people, who might have been of great use to his army as guides, scouts, etc., if he had treated them kindly; but he slighted and neglected them, and they gradually left him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect and properly treat allied or auxiliary forces (e.g., native scouts); neglecting or slighting them risks losing crucial local knowledge and support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delay public rejoicing until military success is certain
rubrics_metrics.description: They came to me with a subscription paper for raising money to defray the expense of a grand firework, which it was intended to exhibit at a rejoicing on receipt of the news of our taking Fort Duquesne. I looked grave, and said it would, I thought, be time enough to prepare for the rejoicing when we knew we should have occasion to rejoice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid public celebratory expenditures or displays before the outcome of uncertain military operations is known; prudence prevents the embarrassment of premature celebration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Militia legislation: accommodate conscientious objectors
rubrics_metrics.description: I had ... drawn a bill for establishing and disciplining of a voluntary militia, which I carried thro' the House without much difficulty, as care was taken in it to leave the Quakers at their liberty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design voluntary militia or civic defense laws that respect religious or conscientious objections (e.g., carve out exemptions) to secure broader acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political conduct: avoid needless disputation to retain goodwill
rubrics_metrics.description: These disputing, contradicting, and confuting people are generally unfortunate in their affairs. They get victory sometimes, but they never get good will, which would be of more use to them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a rule of political or social conduct, avoid engaging in disputation for its own sake because winning arguments may sacrifice useful goodwill and pragmatic support; choose battles carefully to preserve relationships.
